newsitem.title: FRANCE: Peugeot in talks on Brazil car plant.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot in talks on Brazil car plant.

text.p: French carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen is in negotiations to set up production in Brazil, a spokeswoman said on Monday.

"We're in an advanced stage of studies right now, but just studies," the spokeswoman told Reuters. "The breadth of the project hasn't been decided, or the nature, so an investment figure can't be confirmed."

The newspaper La Tribune, citing Brazilian officials, said on Monday the group was in advanced negotiations on a 3.5 billion franc project in Brazil, where many of its competitors, including Renault, have set up production deals.
According to Brazilian newspapers cited by La Tribune, the project would entail the production of engines -- around 150,000 a year -- and the assembly of Peugeot and Citroen cars.
Chairman Jacques Calvet said on October 1 that the group was keen to expand production in Latin America and was considering setting up in Brazil.
"Effectively, we have talked about a project in Brazil," the spokeswoman said. She said the Peugeot group was sending frequent missions to Brazil to study offers from various states.

La Tribune said PSA officials recently met the governor of the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais, Eduardo Azeredo, and Industry and Commerce Minister Mauricio Campos. It said PSA was also looking at the states of Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.
Fiat SpA, Mercedes, Chrysler and Toyota are among the companies building cars or setting up production in Brazil.
Brazilian officials expect the country to be the world's fourth-largest market by the year 2000 with annual production of 2.5 million units.
